+    def _is_unrollable_all_call(self, test):
+        """Return True if `test` is a call to the builtin `all()` with a
+        single generator expression or list comprehension argument and no
+        other arguments, e.g. `all(is_even(x) for x in numbers)`.
+
+        Such calls can be safely unrolled into a for-loop (see
+        `_unroll_all_call` below) to provide much better failure
+        messages, mentioning the offending element instead of just
+        `False`.
+        """
+        return (
+            isinstance(test, ast.Call)
+            and isinstance(test.func, ast.Name)
+            and test.func.id == "all"
+            and len(test.args) == 1
+            and not test.keywords
+            and isinstance(test.args[0], (ast.GeneratorExp, ast.ListComp))
+        )
+
+    def _unroll_all_call(self, call):
+        """Unroll a call of the form `all(<generator or list comprehension>)`
+        into an equivalent for-loop (honouring any nested "for" clauses and
+        "if" conditions of the original comprehension) so that individual
+        assertion failures report the specific element that caused the
+        overall assertion to fail, instead of just reporting that the
+        result of `all(...)` was `False`.  See issue #5062.
+
+        This is only invoked when the `all()` call is the complete
+        condition of an assert statement, see `_is_unrollable_all_call`.
+        """
+        gen_exp = call.args[0]
+        elt = gen_exp.elt
+
+        def build_body(generators_index):
+            if generators_index == len(gen_exp.generators):
+                # We have consumed every "for"/"if" clause of the
+                # comprehension: emit an assert for the element expression,
+                # reusing the regular assertion rewriting logic so we get
+                # the same rich failure messages as a manually written
+                # ``assert elt`` statement would.
+                assertion_module = ast.Module(
+                    body=[ast.Assert(test=elt, msg=None, lineno=1, col_offset=1)]
+                )
+                AssertionRewriter(
+                    module_path=self.module_path, config=self.config
+                ).run(assertion_module)
+                return assertion_module.body
+
+            generator = gen_exp.generators[generators_index]
+            body = build_body(generators_index + 1)
+            # Any "if" conditions on this "for" clause only apply to the
+            # elements they filter, so guard the body with them.
+            for cond in reversed(generator.ifs):
+                body = [ast.If(test=cond, body=body, orelse=[], lineno=1, col_offset=1)]
+            return [
+                ast.For(
+                    target=generator.target,
+                    iter=generator.iter,
+                    body=body,
+                    orelse=[],
+                    lineno=1,
+                    col_offset=1,
+                )
+            ]
+
+        self.statements.extend(build_body(0))
+        # `all()` unrolled into a for-loop that raises on the first failing
+        # element, so if we get here the assertion always succeeded.
+        return _NameConstant(True), ""
+
